title: Mayo Clinic AI-ECG flags low ejection fraction at 97.88%; 41-year-old treated, EF recovers to 55%
summary: At Mayo Clinic two ECGs scored 97.88% and 98.67% for reduced ejection fraction in a 41-year-old with no cardiac history; echo confirmed HFrEF, therapy followed, EF 55% at 4 months. Developer-authored.
account: Harmon, Witt, Friedman and Attia (Cardiovascular Digital Health Journal, 24 August 2021) report a 41-year-old man with class III obesity and sleep apnoea and no cardiac history whose two ECGs, run through Mayo's AI-ECG dashboard, gave probabilities of reduced ejection fraction of 97.88% and 98.67%; echocardiography the next day confirmed reduced function, guideline-directed therapy for new HFrEF was started, and at four months his ejection fraction had improved to 55%, which the authors attribute to therapy, recovery from post-viral sequelae and weight loss. All four authors are at Mayo Clinic, which developed the algorithm and licensed it to Eko and Anumana; Friedman, Attia and other inventors may receive financial benefit. The same developer group published further cases: Dhawan et al. (PACE, 2024) on AI-ECGs predicting left-bundle-branch-block cardiomyopathy six years before presentation, Kenyon et al. (J Pers Med, 2024) on AI-ECG prompting an early AL amyloidosis diagnosis, and Liu et al. (HeartRhythm Case Reports, 2025) on defibrillator decision-making. No source outside Mayo was found for these cases, which is why the earlier verifier set them aside. The date is the publication date.
purpose: Screen 12-lead ECGs for a low left-ventricular ejection fraction with a convolutional neural network
system: Mayo Clinic AI-ECG low-ejection-fraction algorithm (AI-ECG dashboard)
developer: Mayo Clinic (licensed to Eko and Anumana)
segment: Adults presenting with unexplained symptoms and an ECG
taxonomy_note: All case reports are written by the developing institution, with inventors among the authors; no non-developer account exists for this case. Recorded as a benefit with that provenance stated; the three later Mayo cases are listed as echoes.

ratings.reason: New HFrEF identified and treated; ejection fraction 55% at four months.
No organisational outcome reported for this case.

ai_role.statement: The AI-ECG probabilities (97.88% and 98.67%) prompted the echocardiogram and treatment, according to the authors. The source is the developer's own case report; the authors disclose that Mayo licensed the technology and that inventors may receive financial benefit. No independent account of the case exists.
